correctness.rationale: Counting convolution on the full binary group has one eigenvalue per Walsh character, with no scaling. For forbidden run length r, splitting at zeros into runs shorter than r gives the generating series R/(1-zR), where R=sum_{j=0}^{r-1}(uz)^j and u marks ones. At u=1 modulo 2, counts are odd exactly for n congruent to 0 or r modulo r+1; then all Walsh coefficients are odd. At u=-1 the same series gives an exact zero of the full-support Walsh coefficient in every other residue. For r=3 the independent integer replay, with indicator/butterfly and prefix-state checks agreeing on all 16,382 coefficients through n=13, confirms minimum zero degrees 1,1,2,2,2,2,3 at the singular orders 1,2,5,6,9,10,13. It confirms 3,136 allowed words, nullity 1,296, rank 6,896 and the complete stated degree histogram at n=13. The absolute minima in degrees one and two are 274 and 2. The cubic zero supports are exactly (1,7,9), (1,9,11), (3,5,13), (5,7,13). The minimum zero degree is undefined at the nonsingular orders.
residual_risks: The first-minimum-degree and nullity census is finite, for open boundaries. Only the singular-residue criterion has the stated all-length proof.

evidence: The formula covers every open 1^k-avoiding family for k>=2 and n>=1 and every support. Its sharp global minimum nonzero magnitude specializes to 2 at k=3,n=13. Its parity generating function also encodes the full-support coefficient, up to the factor (-1)^n.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier global gap alone would not decide degree-two or cubic zeros; the all-support formula does determine all those values, and the earlier parity calculation also gives the auxiliary singularity test.
